thread:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak to prefer fused-attn on A100s, reranker/embeddings non-chat endpoints saw token/sec drop ~18% on p50 under steady load. Notable: avg batch size fell from 12->8 and KV-cache hit rate dropped ~6%. :eyes:
kevin: ugh. do we have a repro trace? profiler output?
sasha: I pulled a quick perf profile for the 11:30 run. Looks like more short-lived KV entries (eviction count up) and more frequent small batch flushes. snippet:```
batch_formation: samples=22 avg_size=8 median_wait_ms=4
kv: evictions=142 inc_rate=0.28
kernel_choice: fused-attn used 78%
```
ben: interesting — fused-attn selection reduced per-token compute but increased variance in step time for short sequences, which makes batching less effective. KV eviction suggests we might be truncating caches earlier due to token budget policy.
maria: exact hypothesis I had. The new kernel lowers single-request latency but creates more inter-request timing jitter, so continuous-batcher's window closes earlier and we flush smaller batches. For rerankers (many small queries) that kills throughput.
olivia: can we tweak continuous-batcher heuristics instead of reverting kernel change? Ideas: increase token_budget_target for non-chat rerankers, bump max_wait_ms / add aging-priority so older requests get priority to fill batches, or require min_batch_fill before kernel switch heuristics.
kevin: propose experiment: 1) baseline (current) 2) token_budget_target=1.4x + min_batch_fill=6 3) aging_priority: prioritize oldest 30% of queue for early-fill. Measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, batch size distribution, kv hit rate.
sasha: also add a metric for kernel_choice_stability (fraction of batches where kernel changes mid-batch or across close batches) — that might correlate.
ben: command I used to run the load-profile:```bash
./loadtest --workload=rerank-nonchat --qps=350 --seq-len-dist=short-heavy --duration=15m --collect=perf,kv,trace
```
maria: thanks. I'll run the experiments today in staging. One more thing: increase kv-cache TTLs for rerank keys by +30s in staging to see if hit rate recovers; if it does, that points at eviction pressure rather than algorithmic miss.
olivia: small config note — changing token_budget affects memory footprint on GPUs (kv cache size * expected tokens). Flagging infra: @deploy-bot please check capacity headroom before we flip token_budget 1.4x in staging.
deploy-bot: Received. Queuing a capacity check for the staging cluster and will post results in ~10m.
kevin: measurement plan: run A/B for 20m windows, collect batch_size histogram, kv_hit_rate, kernel_fraction, p50/p95 lat, and tail jitter (stddev of inter-arrival at batch start). We'll compare with baseline and pick the lowest cost SLO-compliant config.
sasha: if aging-priority gives similar throughput gains with less kv memory impact, that's ideal. Also let's add a small change to the batching code: avoid closing a batch if (current_size >= min_batch_fill OR oldest_wait_ms >= aging_threshold_ms). That should reduce premature flushes.
ben: agreed. I'll send a tiny PR for that logic after the staging runs. Keep logs small, but include per-batch kernel id and kv_hit_rate for correlation.
maria: ok running first pass now. Will drop results in this thread when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
